subject: Case FaxRxTx / Venali · worldwide fax platform, 2007–2009 · outcome known · test build of the generic report assembler
standfirst: The validation case — the only one this project has with a documented outcome. The chain was run end to end and the number written down and closed before the outcome was opened. A reference-class reading was taken separately, in ignorance of the chain, and lands on the other side of the outcome. This build reproduces the report of 2026-08-26 through the generic assembler; no figure is new.
hint: Two views of the same distributions. Above, how likely each answer is — all curves on one scale, each enclosing the same area. Below, the same thing accumulated: the chance of coming in at or under any figure. Move the pointer and a read line crosses both panels, reporting the chance of exceeding that figure under each instrument. The red bell is the table-priced chain, uncalibrated — Steps B–D never ran on this case — and its width is the rate table's O/M/P spread under a declared ρ = 0.5, a convention. The dotted blue curve is the outside view, a lognormal fitted to its declared quantiles; its tail is drawn to P95 and its P99 is off scale. The two teal curves are the parametric instrument, function points priced on two published effort curves: they sit ×22 below the outcome by design, because they price the functional shell only. The black line is the documented outcome, 120 staffed person-months restated in this unit.
against_outcome_note: Inside the ×1.3 gate. The outcome sits at about P85 of the declared corridor and below the outside view's median.
repeat_note: Two independent size classifications, 87.3% class agreement, priced from the same table: 1 400.4 and 1 446.0 person-days.
outside_note: Funded seats × time, all roles — the same unit the outcome is recorded in; 140 person-months against an outcome of 120.

outcome.lead: This is the only case in the project with a documented outcome, and the only place any of the method's claims can be scored at all.

rows.title: The chain lands inside the ×1.3 gate
rows.text: 11 386 net task hours against an outcome of about 13 304 (120 staffed person-months at the case's own conversion, run 33). The number was written down and closed before the outcome was opened (run 32).

rows.title: The outcome sits at about P85 of the declared corridor
rows.text: The corridor is the rate table's O/M/P spread under ρ = 0.5, a convention; that the outcome falls inside it at P85 is one observation, not a calibration.

rows.title: The outside view lands on the other side
rows.text: The class median, 140 person-months in the unit the outcome is recorded in, is ×1.17 above the outcome where the chain is ×0.86 below it. Neither is averaged.

findings.lead: Produced without being asked for, by instruments whose job was something else.

rows.title: Four elements refused as unsizeable by both repeats
rows.text: A schema that names a platform and not an entity kind, a handler defined by a question, an integration interface with neither direction nor payload, a scope baseline that names no function. Named holes, never guessed (run 31).

rows.title: Function points price the shell
rows.text: 23–27 of 52 obligations sit outside what function points count — telephony, routing, rendering, the points of presence. The parametric instrument's place on this chart is the measure of that.

rows.title: Seven named holes
rows.text: Items the sizing sensors refused to size, listed by the assembly and priced at nothing.

rows.title: No calibration
rows.text: The centre is the table-priced assembly as it stands; the gap-blind rate round and the diagnosis were not run on this case in this generation.

rows.title: The rate table's level
rows.text: Uncalibrated against any outcome; this case is the one place it has been scored, once.
